As for being Reddit light...no, no it's not. Compare the general attitudes of users and I expect you'll find a significant different. Line up some random Reddit and Voat comments and I expect the difference would be clear. We don't seem to like old references, carried on for the sake of it very much, nor "this!" comments that contribute absolutely nothing, or jokes in serious topics. Despite our disagreements in arguments, which can and have gotten very heated, I've seen very little downvoting that was obviously just disagreement. Look at the recent topic about transgenderism for example. The chains in there go on for quite a while because people are actually debating, instead of just steamrolling one opinion over everything else.

Then you have the attitude to voting, which seems to be "only if they deserve it", possibly due to the voting limits, and attitude to moderation, which in some places is so "no censorship" it's actually "no moderation". Contrary to Reddit's policy, the idea of safe spaces is seen here more as an echo chamber, and disliked for it.
